Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers did not just walk out of Pittsburgh. He torched the place on his way out, and now the NFL pregame world is lining up to roast him.
It all started Tuesday night, when the Steelers benched the 42-year-old in favor of backup Mason Rudolph. Rodgers skipped the facility on Wednesday and went straight to The Pat McAfee Show instead. There, he accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of sleeping through meetings. Rodgers' rant occurred on the show, and now FOX & CBS personalities are responding to it.
Steelers legend [Terry Bradshaw went first on FOX,](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dGQK3OaK2lI) leaning on his long friendship with McCarthy and his respect for the Rooney family.
"I'm sorry that Aaron Rodgers had to do this. I'm sorry that he had to go public with all his gripes and complaints. Am I surprised? Absolutely not," Bradshaw said on FOX's pregame show.

He was just getting warmed up, too. Bradshaw called Rodgers "a strange guy" and said athletes never turn on their teammates, coaches, or owners. He even took a parting shot, saying he hopes Rodgers is telling the truth about vanishing from Pittsburgh for good.

Pittsburgh did not wait around. The Steelers cut Rodgers on Wednesday. McCarthy later said things came to a head when Rodgers gave an "ultimatum" that was clearly outside his job description.
A source told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette that Rodgers wanted to call the plays himself. Steelers president Art Rooney II then called it insubordination and said he has full confidence in McCarthy.

# Terry Bradshaw Sides With Mike McCarthy In Aaron Rodgers’ Dispute
The NFL on FOX crew is unanimously backing one side of Aaron Rodgers’ very public feud with his former head coach, Mike McCarthy. Similar to how the Steelers backed McCarthy, everyone on FOX backed the head coach ahead of Thursday’s Eagles vs. Cowboys game on Thanksgiving. That includes a Steelers legend who quarterbacked the franchise to three Super Bowl championships. After McCarthy benched Rodgers on Tuesday in favor of Mason Rudolph, Rodgers didn’t show up to the Steelers’ facility Wednesday morning and later appeared on ESPN’s “The Pat McAfee Show,” exposing McCarthy’s shortcomings this season. “I’m sorry that Aaron Rodgers had to do this. I’m sorry that he had to go public with all his gripes and complaints,” said Terry Bradshaw, who played quarterback for the Steelers from 1970-1983. “Am I surprised? Absolutely not. In my opinion, he’s a strange guy anyway. “The one thing you don’t do — all of us athletes up here — none of us turn on our teammates. We don’t turn on our coaching staff. We don’t turn on our ownership. We show class on our way out. Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that.”

added. The Steelers officially released Rodgers after his interview with McAfee, and he cleared waivers on Thursday, making him an unrestricted free agent. Rodgers was seemingly prepared for that outcome, and wasn’t too concerned, as he said he’s comfortable spewing his gripes because he’s made “$400 million in the NFL.” “You rich jerk,” Strahan said. “You’re a rich bad teammate. … There always seems to be smoke around Aaron Rodgers.” Now that smoke has turned into Rodgers being without a team, midway through what he claimed Wednesday was likely his final NFL season.

Bradshaw, though, wouldn’t mind. “One thing I’m reminded of, Rodgers said, ‘When I’m through playing in Pittsburgh, I’ll disappear, and you’ll never hear from or see me again,'” Bradshaw recalled. “I hope this is the one time he’s telling the truth.”
